prompt: A software company's annual recurring revenue (ARR) grew 30% last year but only 12% this year. The candidate's framework: (1) New customers won; (2) Expansion revenue from existing customers; (3) Revenue lost to churn; (4) Net revenue retention. What is the flaw in this framework?

options.text: Bucket 4 repeats buckets 2 and 3: net retention nets expansion against churn
options.feedback: Right. Net revenue retention is existing customers' revenue after expansion and churn, so bucket 4 counts buckets 2 and 3 again. Keep the three flows: new, expansion, churn.

options.text: Missing: revenue from new customers signed this year
options.feedback: That is bucket 1, new customers won.

options.text: Bucket 1 doesn't belong: new customers don't affect retention
options.feedback: The question is ARR growth, not retention, and new customers are a large part of it.

options.text: It's a generic SaaS dashboard: it never asks why growth slowed
options.feedback: Splitting ARR growth into new, expansion and churn is exactly how to find why it slowed. The flaw is the repeated bucket.

explanation: ARR growth = new + expansion − churn. Net revenue retention is (start + expansion − churn) ÷ start, so it repeats buckets 2 and 3.

extras.corrected_framework: New customers won; expansion from existing customers; churn and downgrades
